notes: MULTI-TAX CASE: two separate taxes (GST 5% and QST 9.975%), both levied on the pre-tax subtotal per current Quebec practice. A scalar tax_amount field cannot represent this; taxes must be a list. A pipeline that captures only one tax will fail subtotal_plus_tax_equals_total.

ROUNDING TRAP (second instance): 2450.00 x 0.09975 = 244.3875 exactly. The invoice shows 244.39, requiring ROUND_HALF_UP. ROUND_HALF_EVEN yields 244.38. Together with the Atlas sales tax this gives two independent documents pinning half-up, which is strong enough to assert in a unit test.

UNIT-BEARING QUANTITY: the migration line reads '4 hrs' in the Qty column. Split into qty '4' plus qty_unit 'hrs' so that 4 x 150.00 = 600.00 still validates. Storing '4 hrs' as a single string breaks the arithmetic check.
Line items have no SKU column, so line matching must fall back to description token-set ratio. sku is explicitly null rather than omitted.

Net 30 from invoice date 2026-07-15 gives exactly 2026-08-14, matching the stated due date. This is a soft cross-check worth running, but a mismatch should warn rather than block since vendors vary on business-day conventions.
Both vendor and customer are in Montreal, and the customer address contains an accented character (Rene-Levesque). Encoding must survive the text path without mojibake.
